1247	// firstDirectRawCharacter scans raw path text as written — without decoding
1248	// percent escapes — and returns the first byte that may not appear directly:
1249	// an ASCII space (U+0020), a C0 control byte (U+0000 through U+001F) or DEL
1250	// (U+007F). Bytes inside a well-formed percent escape ("%" plus two hex
1251	// digits) are skipped, so "%20", "%0A" and "%09" keep parsing and matching
1252	// on the raw encoded form and never register as a direct character; the
1253	// scan never decodes an escape first. A lone or malformed "%" is traversed
1254	// byte by byte here — such an escape is owned by validPercentEscapes, which
1255	// runs before this scan in both readers, and must not let a following
1256	// offending byte be jumped over. It is the one shared decision of the
1257	// request target rule and the route pathPrefix rule, so the two sides that
1258	// must agree on which bytes may appear directly cannot drift apart.
1259	func firstDirectRawCharacter(s string) (byte, bool) {
1260		for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
1261			c := s[i]
1262			if c == '%' && i+2 < len(s) && isHex(s[i+1]) && isHex(s[i+2]) {
1263				i += 2
1264				continue
1265			}
1266			if c == ' ' || c < 0x20 || c == 0x7f {
1267				return c, true
1268			}
1269		}
1270		return 0, false
1271	}

1273	// validateTargetCharacters enforces on the raw target that only percent
1274	// encoding may carry a space or a control character: a direct ASCII space
1275	// (U+0020), a C0 control byte (U+0000 through U+001F) or DEL (U+007F) is
1276	// rejected no matter whether it sits in the path, a parameter name or a
1277	// parameter value. Invalid percent escapes are owned by
1278	// validPercentEscapes, which runs before this check, so a lone or malformed
1279	// "%" keeps its existing reason. The reason names the first offending
1280	// character as U+XXXX.
1281	func validateTargetCharacters(target string) *Failure {
1282		if c, ok := firstDirectRawCharacter(target); ok {
1283			return failuref("invalid_request",
1284				"target contains a character that must be percent-encoded: U+%04X is not allowed to appear directly (percent-encode it, e.g. %%20 for a space)",
1285				c)
1286		}
1287		return nil
1288	}

1290	// isToken reports whether s is an RFC 7230 token, i.e. a legal HTTP method.
1291	func isToken(s string) bool {
1292		if s == "" {
1293			return false
1294		}
1295		for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
1296			if !isTokenChar(s[i]) {
1297				return false
1298			}
1299		}
1300		return true
1301	}

497	// TestQueryTransformRenameChain covers consecutive rename rules: every rule
498	// matches the parameter names that exist when that rule runs — the previous
499	// rename's result — never the request's original names and never a single
500	// simultaneous substitution. Renames also never merge or overwrite colliding
501	// names the way set does.
502	func TestQueryTransformRenameChain(t *testing.T) {
503		cases := []struct {
504			name      string
505			rules     string
506			target    string
507			wantQuery string // expected suffix after http://h.internal/base/p
508		}{
509			{
510				// a=1&b=2&a=3&c=4, a -> b then b -> c: after the first rule the
511				// two former a's are b's, so the second rule renames them together
512				// with the request's original b; its original c keeps its place.
513				name:      "second rename follows the first rename result",
514				rules:     `[{"op":"rename","name":"a","to":"b"},{"op":"rename","name":"b","to":"c"}]`,
515				target:    "/p?a=1&b=2&a=3&c=4",
516				wantQuery: "?c=1&c=2&c=3&c=4",
517			},
518			{
519				// Same two rules in the opposite order: b -> c runs before a ever
520				// becomes b, so the original b alone moves to c and the a's only
521				// move as far as b. Rule order is observable in the output.
522				name:      "swapping the rules changes which names each rule sees",
523				rules:     `[{"op":"rename","name":"b","to":"c"},{"op":"rename","name":"a","to":"b"}]`,
524				target:    "/p?a=1&b=2&a=3&c=4",
525				wantQuery: "?b=1&c=2&b=3&c=4",
526			},
527			{
528				// Three rules forward: every original parameter walks the whole
529				// chain a -> b -> c -> d. A simultaneous rename of the original
530				// names would instead leave three distinct names behind.
531				name:      "three rename rules forward carry every name through",
532				rules:     `[{"op":"rename","name":"a","to":"b"},{"op":"rename","name":"b","to":"c"},{"op":"rename","name":"c","to":"d"}]`,
533				target:    "/p?a=1&b=2&c=3",
534				wantQuery: "?d=1&d=2&d=3",
535			},
536			{
537				// The same three rules in reverse move each name exactly one
538				// step: c -> d runs before b -> c, which runs before a -> b.
539				name:      "three rename rules in reverse move names one step each",
540				rules:     `[{"op":"rename","name":"c","to":"d"},{"op":"rename","name":"b","to":"c"},{"op":"rename","name":"a","to":"b"}]`,
541				target:    "/p?a=1&b=2&c=3",
542				wantQuery: "?b=1&c=2&d=3",
543			},
544			{
545				// Names collide on both hops, including duplicate target-name
546				// parameters: nothing merges or overwrites. Five parameters enter
547				// and five leave, each keeping its position, value and order.
548				name:      "colliding renames keep every parameter in place without merging",
549				rules:     `[{"op":"rename","name":"a","to":"b"},{"op":"rename","name":"b","to":"c"}]`,
550				target:    "/p?b=9&a=1&b=8&a=2&c=0",
551				wantQuery: "?c=9&c=1&c=8&c=2&c=0",
552			},
553			{
554				// Only each hit's name changes: value bytes (lowercase escapes,
555				// '+', extra '='), the valueless form and the empty value's '='
556				// all survive both renames, as do non-hit parameters.
557				name:      "chained renames keep value bytes and both empty forms",
558				rules:     `[{"op":"rename","name":"a","to":"b"},{"op":"rename","name":"b","to":"c"}]`,
559				target:    "/p?a=%2f+%2F+a=b&a&a=&x=1",
560				wantQuery: "?c=%2f+%2F+a=b&c&c=&x=1",
561			},
562			{
563				// Empty fragments and non-hit parameters keep their bytes and
564				// positions while the hits walk both rules.
565				name:      "chained renames leave empty fragments and misses as is",
566				rules:     `[{"op":"rename","name":"a","to":"b"},{"op":"rename","name":"b","to":"c"}]`,
567				target:    "/p?z=0&&a=1&&b=2&",
568				wantQuery: "?z=0&&c=1&&c=2&",
569			},
570			{
571				// A first rule with no source changes nothing and must not
572				// re-encode existing names (the raw '+' stays a '+'), and later
573				// rules still run: a walks to b and then c while "a b" never
574				// matches a rule looking for "a".
575				name:      "a no-hit rule neither re-encodes nor stops later rules",
576				rules:     `[{"op":"rename","name":"z","to":"q"},{"op":"rename","name":"a","to":"b"},{"op":"rename","name":"b","to":"c"}]`,
577				target:    "/p?a=1&a+b=2&a%20b=3",
578				wantQuery: "?c=1&a+b=2&a%20b=3",
579			},
580			{
581				// A rule renaming a name to itself is a byte-for-byte no-op (no
582				// re-encoding of either space spelling) and must not break the
583				// chain: the later rules still run on their results.
584				name:      "a self-rename step neither re-encodes nor stops later rules",
585				rules:     `[{"op":"rename","name":"a b","to":"a b"},{"op":"rename","name":"a","to":"b"},{"op":"rename","name":"b","to":"c"}]`,
586				target:    "/p?a=1&a+b=2&a%20b=3",
587				wantQuery: "?c=1&a+b=2&a%20b=3",
588			},
589			{
590				name:      "chained renames with no query string do not create a mark",
591				rules:     `[{"op":"rename","name":"a","to":"b"},{"op":"rename","name":"b","to":"c"}]`,
592				target:    "/p",
593				wantQuery: "",
594			},
595			{
596				name:      "chained renames with an empty question mark keep it",
597				rules:     `[{"op":"rename","name":"a","to":"b"},{"op":"rename","name":"b","to":"c"}]`,
598				target:    "/p?",
599				wantQuery: "?",
600			},
601		}
602		for _, tc := range cases {
603			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
604				got := transformResult(t, tc.rules, tc.target)
605				want := buildWant(tc.target, tc.wantQuery)
606				if got != want {
607					t.Errorf("upstreamURL = %q, want %q", got, want)
608				}
609			})
610		}
611	}

613	// TestQueryTransformRenameChainEncodedIntermediateNames covers chains whose
614	// intermediate name needs encoding: the next rule uses that name as a literal
615	// and must still hit the renamed parameters. It also pins the name-comparison
616	// rules across a chain boundary: '+' and "%20" in a request name both denote a
617	// space, a literal '+' is a different name, and matching stays case-sensitive.
618	func TestQueryTransformRenameChainEncodedIntermediateNames(t *testing.T) {
619		cases := []struct {
620			name      string
621			rules     string
622			target    string
623			wantQuery string
624		}{
625			{
626				// a becomes the space-bearing name "x y" (encoded x%20y by rule
627				// one); rule two names "x y" as a literal and matches the decoded
628				// intermediate, moving it on to z.
629				name:      "space intermediate name is matched as a literal by the next rule",
630				rules:     `[{"op":"rename","name":"a","to":"x y"},{"op":"rename","name":"x y","to":"z"}]`,
631				target:    "/p?a=1",
632				wantQuery: "?z=1",
633			},
634			{
635				// '+' and "%20" in the request both decode to a space, so the
636				// m+n and m%20n parameters join the renamed a under the literal
637				// intermediate name "m n" and all move to z. A literal '+' name
638				// (m%2Bn) is a different parameter and is left untouched.
639				name:      "plus and percent-space request names both reach the space intermediate",
640				rules:     `[{"op":"rename","name":"a","to":"m n"},{"op":"rename","name":"m n","to":"z"}]`,
641				target:    "/p?a=1&m%20n=9&m+n=8&m%2Bn=7",
642				wantQuery: "?z=1&z=9&z=8&m%2Bn=7",
643			},
644			{
645				// The intermediate name contains a literal '+', encoded as %2B by
646				// rule one. Rule two's literal "p+q" hits the renamed a and the
647				// request's p%2Bq; the request's raw p+q (a space name) does not
648				// match and stays written with its '+'.
649				name:      "literal-plus intermediate matches encoded plus, not a space spelling",
650				rules:     `[{"op":"rename","name":"a","to":"p+q"},{"op":"rename","name":"p+q","to":"z"}]`,
651				target:    "/p?a=1&p%2Bq=2&p+q=3",
652				wantQuery: "?z=1&z=2&p+q=3",
653			},
654			{
655				// A non-ASCII intermediate name with a space: the request's
656				// percent-encoded same-name parameter joins the renamed a at rule
657				// one and both move on at rule two.
658				name:      "chinese intermediate name continues the chain",
659				rules:     `[{"op":"rename","name":"a","to":"中 文"},{"op":"rename","name":"中 文","to":"z"}]`,
660				target:    "/p?a=1&%E4%B8%AD%20%E6%96%87=2",
661				wantQuery: "?z=1&z=2",
662			},
663			{
664				// Case sensitivity holds at every hop: a -> B creates uppercase B,
665				// so b -> c only moves the lowercase original; both uppercase B's
666				// remain.
667				name:      "name comparison stays case sensitive along the chain",
668				rules:     `[{"op":"rename","name":"a","to":"B"},{"op":"rename","name":"b","to":"c"}]`,
669				target:    "/p?a=1&b=2&B=3",
670				wantQuery: "?B=1&c=2&B=3",
671			},
672		}
673		for _, tc := range cases {
674			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
675				got := transformResult(t, tc.rules, tc.target)
676				want := buildWant(tc.target, tc.wantQuery)
677				if got != want {
678					t.Errorf("upstreamURL = %q, want %q", got, want)
679				}
680			})
681		}
682	}

684	// TestQueryTransformRenameChainInvalidEscapeStillRejected pins that a rename
685	// chain can never launder a malformed percent escape into an accepted request:
686	// all names are decoded before any rule runs, so renaming the carrying
687	// parameter later cannot make the request valid, and no partially chained query
688	// may come back as a success.
689	func TestQueryTransformRenameChainInvalidEscapeStillRejected(t *testing.T) {
690		cfg := transformConfig(t, `[{"op":"rename","name":"a","to":"b"},{"op":"rename","name":"b","to":"c"}]`)
691		targets := []string{
692			"/p?a=1&b%zz=2",     // rule two would rename the bad name away
693			"/p?b%zz=2&a=1",     // bad name before a parameter rule one renames
694			"/p?a%zz=1",         // rule one would rename the bad name itself
695			"/p?a=1&b%zz=2&c=4", // bad name among parameters that rename fine
696			"/p?a=1&b=2%2",      // truncated escape in a value the chain carries
697		}
698		for _, target := range targets {
699			// The front door: ParseRequest rejects the target outright no matter
700			// what the chain would have done with it.
701			_, rf := ParseRequest([]byte(`{"method":"GET","target":"` + target + `"}`))
702			if rf == nil || rf.Code != "invalid_request" {
703				t.Fatalf("ParseRequest(%q): got %+v, want invalid_request", target, rf)
704			}
705		}
706	
707		// A caller that bypasses ParseRequest still gets invalid_request from
708		// Resolve whenever the malformed escape sits in a decoded name — names
709		// are all decoded up front, before the first rename — and never a partial
710		// Resolution.
711		for _, target := range []string{
712			"/p?a=1&b%zz=2",
713			"/p?b%zz=2&a=1",
714			"/p?a%zz=1",
715			"/p?a=1&b%zz=2&c=4",
716		} {
717			res, rf := Resolve(cfg, &Request{Method: "GET", Target: target})
718			if rf == nil || rf.Code != "invalid_request" {
719				t.Fatalf("Resolve(%q): got %+v, want invalid_request", target, rf)
720			}
721			if res != nil {
722				t.Fatalf("Resolve(%q): got partial success %+v, want no resolution", target, res)
723			}
724		}
725	}

728	// Resolution: chained renames are query content only, so route selection and
729	// upstream path joining are exactly what they are without rules, and a route
730	// without transforms keeps the identical query byte for byte.
731	func TestQueryTransformRenameChainKeepsRoutingAndJoin(t *testing.T) {

766	// buildWant joins the expected query suffix onto the transformed target path.
767	func buildWant(target, wantQuery string) string {
768		base := "http://h.internal/base"
769		path := target
770		if q := strings.IndexByte(target, '?'); q >= 0 {
771			path = target[:q]
772		}
773		return base + path + wantQuery
774	}

1	// Regression coverage for the copy rule when parameter names themselves
2	// contain '&', '=' or a literal '%'. These characters are content inside a
3	// name, never query-string structure: a raw '&' is the only fragment
4	// separator and only the first raw '=' of a fragment splits its name from the
5	// value, while the configured name and "to" are used literally. Every case
6	// below goes through the public entry points — ParseConfig for reading the
7	// configuration and ParseRequest/Resolve for reading a request and obtaining
8	// a resolution — so it pins user-observable behavior rather than the internal
9	// rewriter.
10	package contractsentinel
11	
12	import (
13		"strings"
14		"testing"
15	)
16	
17	// TestQueryTransformCopySpecialCharNames copies names that literally carry
18	// '&', '=' or '%'. The request spellings use percent escapes for those bytes
19	// (a raw '&' or '=' could never sit inside one name), the request name is
20	// decoded exactly once for comparison, and the copy's new name is rendered the
21	// way set encodes a name. Sources keep their raw name spelling, position and
22	// value; each copy lands immediately after its own source; parameters already
23	// carrying the target name stay where they are, neither merged nor
24	// overwritten; and a source's first '=' plus everything after it is copied
25	// byte for byte.
26	func TestQueryTransformCopySpecialCharNames(t *testing.T) {
27		cases := []struct {
28			name      string
29			rules     string
30			target    string
31			wantQuery string // expected suffix after http://h.internal/base/p
32		}{
33			{
34				// The headline case. Both hex casings of the source name
35				// ("a%26b%3dc" and "a%26b%3Dc") decode to "a&b=c" and each gains
36				// its own copy right behind it. The copy name "x=y&z" is rendered
37				// as "x%3dy%26z", so it can never split into extra fragments; the
38				// pre-existing x%3dy%26z=9 stays in place (no merge, no overwrite).
39				// The first source's value keeps its extra '=', lowercase escape,
40				// uppercase escape and '+' byte for byte; the empty value keeps
41				// its '='; the valueless source gains a valueless copy; the
42				// unrelated parameters, raw encoding and trailing empty fragment
43				// all keep their bytes and order.
44				name:   "ampersand and equals in both names are content, not structure",
45				rules:  `[{"op":"copy","name":"a&b=c","to":"x=y&z"}]`,
46				target: "/p?keep=%2f+&a%26b%3dc=1=%2f+%2F&x%3dy%26z=9&a%26b%3Dc=&a%26b%3Dc&&z=z",
47				wantQuery: "?keep=%2f+&a%26b%3dc=1=%2f+%2F&x%3Dy%26z=1=%2f+%2F" +
48					"&x%3dy%26z=9&a%26b%3Dc=&x%3Dy%26z=&a%26b%3Dc&x%3Dy%26z&&z=z",
49			},
50			{
51				// Lowercase and uppercase percent escapes denote the same decoded
52				// source name; duplicates in different positions are copied
53				// independently and the unrelated fragment between them is
54				// unmoved.
55				name:      "lowercase and uppercase hex source spellings each get a copy",
56				rules:     `[{"op":"copy","name":"a&b=c","to":"x=y&z"}]`,
57				target:    "/p?a%26b%3dc=1&b=0&a%26b%3Dc=2",
58				wantQuery: "?a%26b%3dc=1&x%3Dy%26z=1&b=0&a%26b%3Dc=2&x%3Dy%26z=2",
59			},
60			{
61				// A source without '=' produces a copy without '='; an empty value
62				// keeps its '=' in the copy; the source's own spelling is
63				// untouched.
64				name:      "valueless special source stays valueless and empty value keeps equals",
65				rules:     `[{"op":"copy","name":"a&b=c","to":"x=y&z"}]`,
66				target:    "/p?a%26b%3Dc&a%26b%3Dc=&x=1",
67				wantQuery: "?a%26b%3Dc&x%3Dy%26z&a%26b%3Dc=&x%3Dy%26z=&x=1",
68			},
69			{
70				// The fragment "a=b=1" is split at its first raw '=', so its name
71				// is "a" and its value is "b=1". The literal rule name "a=b" must
72				// not match it: nothing is copied and the bytes are unchanged.
73				name:      "first raw equals splits, so a=b=1 is not a parameter named a=b",
74				rules:     `[{"op":"copy","name":"a=b","to":"c"}]`,
75				target:    "/p?a=b=1",
76				wantQuery: "?a=b=1",
77			},
78			{
79				// The positive contrast: an encoded '=' inside the request name
80				// decodes to the literal '=' the rule names, so that parameter is
81				// the source while "a=b=1" (whose name is just "a") is left alone.
82				name:      "encoded equals in the request name matches the literal rule name",
83				rules:     `[{"op":"copy","name":"a=b","to":"c"}]`,
84				target:    "/p?a=b=1&a%3Db=2",
85				wantQuery: "?a=b=1&a%3Db=2&c=2",
86			},
87			{
88				// The rule name is the literal text "%26" — percent, 2, 6. A
89				// request name is decoded only once, so "%2526" (which decodes to
90				// "%26") is the hit while "%26" (which decodes to "&") is a
91				// different parameter and is left untouched.
92				name:      "literal percent-escape rule name matches only the double-encoded form",
93				rules:     `[{"op":"copy","name":"%26","to":"c"}]`,
94				target:    "/p?%26=1&%2526=2",
95				wantQuery: "?%26=1&%2526=2&c=2",
96			},
97			{
98				// Copying onto the literal name "%26" must render a double-encoded
99				// copy name ("%2526"), never bytes that a parser would read as the
100				// separator '&'. The existing "%26" parameter (whose decoded name
101				// is "&") stays in place and is not treated as the same target.
102				name:      "copy onto a literal percent-escape name is double encoded",
103				rules:     `[{"op":"copy","name":"a","to":"%26"}]`,
104				target:    "/p?a=1&%26=9",
105				wantQuery: "?a=1&%2526=1&%26=9",
106			},
107			{
108				// A bare literal percent in the target name is percent-encoded
109				// like any other non-unreserved byte, as set does.
110				name:      "literal percent in the target name is encoded as percent 25",
111				rules:     `[{"op":"copy","name":"a","to":"100%"}]`,
112				target:    "/p?a=1",
113				wantQuery: "?a=1&100%25=1",
114			},
115			{
116				// A name with a literal percent and an encoded '=': only
117				// "a%25b%3dc" (decoding once to "a%b=c") matches. The other
118				// spelling decodes one level deeper ("a%b%3Dc"), is a different
119				// parameter and stays put, and no copy's bytes can introduce a
120				// structural separator.
121				name:      "literal percent together with encoded equals matches one decoding level",
122				rules:     `[{"op":"copy","name":"a%b=c","to":"d%26e"}]`,
123				target:    "/p?a%25b%3dc=1&a%25b%253Dc=2",
124				wantQuery: "?a%25b%3dc=1&d%2526e=1&a%25b%253Dc=2",
125			},
126			{
127				// With no hit the query is preserved byte for byte, the trailing
128				// empty fragment included.
129				name:      "absent special source name changes nothing including the empty fragment",
130				rules:     `[{"op":"copy","name":"z&z","to":"c"}]`,
131				target:    "/p?a%26b%3dc=1&",
132				wantQuery: "?a%26b%3dc=1&",
133			},
134			{
135				// Sanity on the structural boundary: "a=1&b=2" holds two
136				// parameters named "a" and "b", never one parameter whose name
137				// contains '&', so a rule naming "a&b" cannot match.
138				name:      "a raw separator never becomes part of a name",
139				rules:     `[{"op":"copy","name":"a&b","to":"c"}]`,
140				target:    "/p?a=1&b=2",
141				wantQuery: "?a=1&b=2",
142			},
143		}
144		for _, tc := range cases {
145			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
146				got := transformResult(t, tc.rules, tc.target)
147				want := buildWant(tc.target, tc.wantQuery)
148				if got != want {
149					t.Errorf("upstreamURL = %q, want %q", got, want)
150				}
151			})
152		}
153	}
154	
155	// TestQueryTransformCopyThenRemoveSpecialCharNames runs the rules strictly in
156	// configured order: copying "a&b=c" onto "x=y&z" and then removing "x=y&z"
157	// deletes both the freshly inserted copies and the request's original
158	// parameters of that target name, while the sources survive with their
159	// original name encodings (lowercase and uppercase alike) and every other
160	// fragment keeps its bytes and order.
161	func TestQueryTransformCopyThenRemoveSpecialCharNames(t *testing.T) {
162		rules := `[
163		  {"op":"copy","name":"a&b=c","to":"x=y&z"},
164		  {"op":"remove","name":"x=y&z"}
165		]`
166		target := "/p?keep=%2f+&a%26b%3dc=1=%2f+%2F&x%3dy%26z=9&a%26b%3Dc=&a%26b%3Dc&&z=z"
167		got := transformResult(t, rules, target)
168		wantQuery := "?keep=%2f+&a%26b%3dc=1=%2f+%2F&a%26b%3Dc=&a%26b%3Dc&&z=z"
169		if want := buildWant(target, wantQuery); got != want {
170			t.Fatalf("upstreamURL = %q, want %q", got, want)
171		}
172	}
173	
174	// TestQueryTransformCopySpecialNamesKeepsRoutingAndJoin asserts on the whole
175	// Resolution: special characters in copy names are query content only, so
176	// route selection and upstream path joining stay exactly what they are without
177	// rules, and a request landing on a transform-free route is preserved byte for
178	// byte.
179	func TestQueryTransformCopySpecialNamesKeepsRoutingAndJoin(t *testing.T) {
180		cfg := mustConfig(t, `{"routes":[
181		  {"id":"api","methods":["GET"],"pathPrefix":"/api","upstream":"http://api.internal/v1",
182		   "queryTransforms":[{"op":"copy","name":"a&b=c","to":"x=y&z"}]},
183		  {"id":"root","methods":["*"],"pathPrefix":"/","upstream":"http://root.internal"}
184		]}`)
185	
186		res := resolveJSON(t, cfg, `{"method":"GET","target":"/api/orders/7?a%26b%3dc=1&x%3dy%26z=9"}`)
187		if res.RouteID != "api" {
188			t.Errorf("routeId = %q, want api", res.RouteID)
189		}
190		if want := "http://api.internal/v1/orders/7?a%26b%3dc=1&x%3Dy%26z=1&x%3dy%26z=9"; res.UpstreamURL != want {
191			t.Errorf("upstreamURL = %q, want %q", res.UpstreamURL, want)
192		}
193	
194		// On the transform-free route the same query survives unchanged.
195		res = resolveJSON(t, cfg, `{"method":"GET","target":"/other?a%26b%3dc=1&x%3dy%26z=9"}`)
196		if res.RouteID != "root" {
197			t.Errorf("routeId = %q, want root", res.RouteID)
198		}
199		if want := "http://root.internal/other?a%26b%3dc=1&x%3dy%26z=9"; res.UpstreamURL != want {
200			t.Errorf("upstreamURL = %q, want %q", res.UpstreamURL, want)
201		}
202	}
203	
204	// TestQueryTransformCopySpecialNamesRoundTrip saves a configuration whose copy
205	// rules carry '&', '=' and '%' in their literal names and re-reads it: the
206	// literal rule strings and the rule order survive (ampersand is allowed to
207	// appear only as a JSON escape such as \u0026 in the saved text), and the same
208	// request resolves to the same routeId and upstreamURL before and after the
209	// save.
210	func TestQueryTransformCopySpecialNamesRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
211		cfg := mustConfig(t, `{"routes":[{"id":"r1","methods":["*"],"pathPrefix":"/","upstream":"http://h.internal/base",
212		  "queryTransforms":[
213		    {"op":"copy","name":"a&b=c","to":"x=y&z"},
214		    {"op":"copy","name":"%26","to":"q"},
215		    {"op":"remove","name":"x=y&z"}
216		  ]}]}`)
217	
218		doc := string(mustMarshal(t, cfg))
219		for _, want := range []string{
220			`"name":"a\u0026b=c"`,
221			`"to":"x=y\u0026z"`,
222			`"name":"%26"`,
223			`{"op":"remove","name":"x=y\u0026z"}`,
224		} {
225			if !strings.Contains(doc, want) {
226				t.Fatalf("saved config missing %q:\n%s", want, doc)
227			}
228		}
229	
230		// a&b=c is copied onto x=y&z, "%26" (hit via the double-encoded %2526) is
231		// copied onto q, and the final remove clears every x=y&z parameter — the
232		// fresh copies and the pre-existing one alike.
233		target := "/p?a%26b%3dc=1&%2526=2&x%3dy%26z=8&keep=+"
234		after, _ := roundTripResolve(t, cfg, "GET", target)
235		want := "http://h.internal/base/p?a%26b%3dc=1&%2526=2&q=2&keep=+"
236		if after.UpstreamURL != want {
237			t.Fatalf("upstreamURL = %q, want %q", after.UpstreamURL, want)
238		}
239	}
240	
241	// TestQueryTransformCopySpecialNamesInvalidEscapeStillRejected pins that no
242	// copy chain can launder a malformed percent escape: request names are all
243	// decoded up front, before any rule runs, so a truncated or non-hex escape
244	// fails the request as invalid_request even when a later rule would delete the
245	// carrying parameter. ParseRequest hands back no usable request, and a caller
246	// resolving an in-process request with a bad escape in a name gets no partial
247	// Resolution.
248	func TestQueryTransformCopySpecialNamesInvalidEscapeStillRejected(t *testing.T) {
249		cfg := transformConfig(t, `[
250		  {"op":"copy","name":"a&b=c","to":"x=y&z"},
251		  {"op":"remove","name":"x=y&z"},
252		  {"op":"remove","name":"bad"}
253		]`)
254	
255		// Every target is rejected at the front door regardless of what the later
256		// rules would have done with the carrying fragment.
257		parseTargets := []struct {
258			target string
259			where  string
260		}{
261			{"/p?a%26b%zz=1", "non-hex escape inside the source name itself"},
262			{"/p?a%26b%3=1", "truncated escape inside the source name itself"},
263			{"/p?bad%zz=2&a%26b%3dc=1", "non-hex name a later remove would delete"},
264			{"/p?a%26b%3dc=1&other%2", "truncated escape in another name"},
265			{"/p?a%26b%3dc=1&keep=1%2", "truncated escape in a value the copy carries"},
266		}
267		for _, tc := range parseTargets {
268			t.Run("parse: "+tc.where, func(t *testing.T) {
269				req, rf := ParseRequest([]byte(`{"method":"GET","target":"` + tc.target + `"}`))
270				if rf == nil || rf.Code != "invalid_request" {
271					t.Fatalf("ParseRequest(%q): got %+v, want invalid_request", tc.target, rf)
272				}
273				if !strings.Contains(rf.Reason, "percent escape") {
274					t.Fatalf("ParseRequest(%q): reason = %q, want it to explain the bad percent escape", tc.target, rf.Reason)
275				}
276				if req != nil {
277					t.Fatalf("ParseRequest(%q): got a usable request %+v alongside the failure", tc.target, req)
278				}
279			})
280		}
281	
282		// A caller that bypasses ParseRequest still fails when the bad escape sits
283		// in a decoded name — names are decoded before the first copy — and never
284		// receives a partial success, even though the later remove rules would
285		// have removed the offending fragments.
286		for _, target := range []string{
287			"/p?a%26b%zz=1",
288			"/p?a%26b%3=1",
289			"/p?bad%zz=2&a%26b%3dc=1",
290			"/p?a%26b%3dc=1&other%2",
291		} {
292			t.Run("resolve: "+target, func(t *testing.T) {
293				res, rf := Resolve(cfg, &Request{Method: "GET", Target: target})
294				if rf == nil || rf.Code != "invalid_request" {
295					t.Fatalf("Resolve(%q): got %+v, want invalid_request", target, rf)
296				}
297				if !strings.Contains(rf.Reason, "percent escape") {
298					t.Fatalf("Resolve(%q): reason = %q, want it to explain the bad percent escape", target, rf.Reason)
299				}
300				if res != nil {
301					t.Fatalf("Resolve(%q): got partial success %+v, want no resolution", target, res)
302				}
303			})
304		}

## 新增文件

**`contractsentinel/query_copy_special_names_test.go`** — 针对公开 API（`ParseConfig` 读配置、`ParseRequest`/`Resolve` 读请求并取得解析结果）：

- **`TestQueryTransformCopySpecialCharNames`**（11 个表驱动用例）
  - 头条场景：规则名 `a&b=c` 复制为 `x=y&z`，请求中 `a%26b%3dc` 与 `a%26b%3Dc`（大小写十六进制）都命中、各产生一个紧跟来源的副本；来源保留原始名称编码/位置/值；新名称写成 `x%3Dy%26z`；已有同名目标参数留在原处不合并不覆盖；值中的 `+`、百分号大小写、额外 `=` 逐字节保留；无等号来源生成无等号副本、空值保留等号；未命中参数与空片段保持字节和顺序。
  - `a=b=1` 的名称是 `a`（首个原始 `=` 切分），不命中 `a=b` 规则；对照用例确认 `a%3Db` 才命中。
  - 名称比较只解码一次：规则名 `%26` 只复制 `%2526`、不复制 `%26`；复制为字面量 `%26` 时副本名写成 `%2526`，不会变成分隔符；字面 `%` 编码为 `%25`；原始 `&` 永不并入名称。
- **`TestQueryTransformCopyThenRemoveSpecialCharNames`**：先 `copy a&b=c→x=y&z` 再 `remove x=y&z`，删除新副本与原有同名目标参数，保留来源（两种原始编码）及其他内容。
- **`TestQueryTransformCopySpecialNamesKeepsRoutingAndJoin`**：routeId 与上游路径拼接不受影响，无规则路由逐字节保留。
- **`TestQueryTransformCopySpecialNamesRoundTrip`**：含 `&`/`=`/`%` 字面值的规则保存回 JSON（库层 `&` 写为 `\u0026`）再读取，语义一致。
- **`TestQueryTransformCopySpecialNamesInvalidEscapeStillRejected`**：名称/值中含非十六进制或截断的百分号转义时，即使后续 `remove` 会删除该参数，`ParseRequest` 与绕过它的 `Resolve` 都返回带原因说明的 `invalid_request`，不留下任何成功结果。

**`cmd/contractsentinel/resolve_copy_special_names_cli_test.go`** — 以 README 描述的真实使用边界端到端复现（配置文件 + stdin JSON）：头条字节级场景、单次解码/双编码名称比较、copy→remove 规则顺序，以及坏转义时 exit 非零、stdout 全空、stderr 单个 `invalid_request` JSON。

```

```
